clue.text: Influential politician, note, has rejected diplomacy

parts.note: FA is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: rejected suggests the word for diplomacy is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: A powerful politician with a musical note has given up on being diplomatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a sol-fa syllable here, not a written message; 'has rejected' reads the diplomacy word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is slang for a wealthy, powerful figure, such as a highly paid party grandee.

clue.text: Options include cold treats from the freezer

indicators.note: include means the word for options takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: choices are options
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A menu of frozen desserts offers several choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc ices are ice-cream bars coated in chocolate, a British freezer staple.

clue.text: Jazz musician, somebody that can hold a note

indicators.note: a word able to hold another has that other placed within it

parts.note: a person is somebody
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A jazz player is praised as someone who can sustain a long note.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist.

clue.text: Regular route finally barred, on going beyond river

indicators.note: going beyond means coming after the river abbreviation in the answer
the final letter of the word for route is barred, kept out

parts.note: a path is a route

explanation.surface: A regular commuter finds the end of the route closed off beyond the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular customer of a shop or pub is its patron.

clue.text: British leader detains evil commander over irreligious practices

indicators.note: detains means the leader's abbreviation holds the following pieces inside

parts.note: PM, Prime Minister, is the British leader
an aga is a Turkish commander

indicators.note: over signals that the word for evil is turned back

parts.note: sin is evil

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister locks up a wicked general accused of godless rites.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is an old Ottoman title, a crossword favourite; 'over' reverses only the evil word before both go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism covers beliefs and rites outside the major world religions, hence irreligious practices.

clue.text: Brilliant achievement for rower

definitions.meaning: a ... of genius is a brilliant achievement
the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace of a crew

explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is both a masterly feat and the pace-setting oarsman in a rowing eight.

clue.text: Presumably least able to afford medical procedure?

definitions.meaning: skint is British slang for broke, and the playful superlative means most broke
a test of allergy or reaction made on the patient's skin

explanation.surface: Whoever is poorest is unlikely to be able to pay for a medical check.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money; the clue treats SKINTEST as its superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin test checks for allergies or infection by applying a substance to the skin.

clue.text: Some characters in race definitely give up

indicators.note: Some characters in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A runner certainly gives up partway through the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or give up territory or a claim.

clue.text: Openings of books like Ulysses: extremely coarse

indicators.note: openings are first letters, taken from each of the following words

explanation.surface: Novels such as Joyce's Ulysses are judged to be very crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses, James Joyce's novel, was once banned as obscene, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are coarse and smutty.

clue.text: Impressing kid, drive with champion in motor event

indicators.note: impressing means pressing a piece into the middle of the others

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for Drive in street names
to kid or rag someone is to tease them
an ace is a champion

explanation.surface: A champion driver keeps teasing a youngster at the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short straight-line acceleration contest between cars.

clue.text: Force states to surrender capital, when in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the capital, the first letter, is surrendered

parts.note: to assert is to state

explanation.surface: Countries are compelled to give up their capital cities when beaten back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to surrender capital' cuts ASSERTS to SSERTS; 'when in retreat' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress in physics and engineering is force applied over an area.

clue.text: Reached a dry area in central Sweden

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

indicators.note: central picks out the two middle letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: Someone arrived at an alcohol-free region in the middle of Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attained a goal is to have reached it.

clue.text: Leave as arranged

definitions.meaning: to set off on a journey
laid out or displayed in order

explanation.definitionFit: Set out means both to depart and to have been laid out in order.

clue.text: Wine limited, we're told, in old Christian festival

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: we're told signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: tied means restricted or limited

explanation.surface: Wine was rationed at an ancient church celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Hocktide was a medieval English festival held after Easter.

clue.text: Voting expert identified Liberals in advert

indicators.note: in means the Liberals go inside the advertisement word

parts.note: a poster is an advert
L is Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A polling analyst spotted Liberal party members in a campaign advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollster conducts opinion polls, measuring how people intend to vote.

clue.text: Wow — caught transport in snowbound area

indicators.note: caught by the ear, something heard rather than read

parts.note: to slay an audience is to wow them

explanation.surface: An amazed exclamation at seeing a vehicle in the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer over snow.

clue.text: Friendly cop intervenes in a brief set-to

indicators.note: intervening puts the cop word between other letters
brief means the last letter is cut

parts.note: a melee is a confused fight, a set-to
to nab is to cop or catch

explanation.surface: A friendly policeman steps into a short scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a noun for a policeman but is the verb meaning catch; 'brief' trims the last letter of the fight word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is agreeable and willing to cooperate, so friendly in manner.

clue.text: Crack about churchman with no time for blessing

parts.note: C, circa, means about
Rev, Reverend, is a churchman

indicators.note: no time means the abbreviation T for time is removed

parts.note: an asset is a blessing or benefit

explanation.surface: A clergyman cracks under pressure, having no time to give a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' drops T from ASSET to give ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier.

clue.text: Witness determined to stand up if concealed by row of seats

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: set means determined

indicators.note: concealed by means put inside the following word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A witness resolved to stand in court, though hidden behind the seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stand up' turns SET to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: A testifier is one who gives evidence, a witness.

clue.text: Film-maker hampering actor desperate to land role at last

indicators.note: desperate suggests a wild state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A desperate actor gets in the way of a director while hoping for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to land' means take in the last letter of 'role', E, which joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the director of photography on a film.

clue.text: Bird turned tail, hiding in shelter

indicators.note: hiding in means the jumbled letters go inside the shelter word

parts.note: a cot is a small shelter, as in dovecot

indicators.note: turned means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird turned tail and hid in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small British songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Officer said to support my promotion, initially

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like my!

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter

parts.note: oral means spoken, said

explanation.surface: An officer is said to back the narrator's promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer in the army.

clue.text: Judge feeling heartless

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling

explanation.surface: A judge is accused of lacking any compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle I out of SENTIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence is to pass judgement on a convicted person, as a judge does.

clue.text: Slave has fight with historian, losing it

parts.note: to spar is to fight

indicators.note: losing means the letters are dropped from the historian's name

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slave quarrels with a historian, losing the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes IT from TACITUS to leave TACUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Investigates exploits covered up by fellow

indicators.note: covered by the fellow means placed inside that word

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A man looks into dealings that someone has hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploits' looks like a noun meaning deeds but is the verb; 'up' reverses it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase up a matter is to pursue or look into it.

clue.text: Papal edict subsequently circulated, after year end?

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: Dec, December, is the year's end

indicators.note: circulated means turned round

parts.note: later means subsequently

explanation.surface: A papal decree is issued later, at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A decretal is a papal decree settling a point of church law.

clue.text: Make small dish to hold one tart without filling

indicators.note: to hold means taking the next pieces inside

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, a belle
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: without filling means the middle letters are removed

parts.note: taken as a word to be emptied

explanation.surface: A recipe: a dish holding a tart without any filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for a good-looking person, not crockery; 'without filling' empties the tart to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to make something seem small or unimportant.

clue.text: Loser grounded after trouncing

indicators.note: trouncing is a beating, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A defeated team is grounded after a heavy loss.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the competitor expected to lose.

clue.text: In debate, summit's leaders will go round in circles

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for circles

parts.note: discs are circles

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: the leading letters of the word summit are S and U

explanation.surface: In talks, the summit leaders keep going round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' here means the first two letters of summit; 'will go round' reverses them before they sit in the circles word.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a matter is to discuss it, talk it over.
